{"questions": [

"topic": "number theory: modular arithmetic and residues (divisibility via polynomial remainder)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Find the sum of the positive integers n such that n + 1 divides n^2 + 71.",
"answer": 183,
"target_wrong": 175,
"error_description": "The divisor 9 of 72 is left out of the list of divisors of 72, so the solution n = 8 is missing.",
"cases": ["n+1=2, n=1", "n+1=3, n=2", "n+1=4, n=3", "n+1=6, n=5", "n+1=8, n=7", "n+1=9, n=8", "n+1=12, n=11", "n+1=18, n=17", "n+1=24, n=23", "n+1=36, n=35", "n+1=72, n=71"],
"solution": "Since n^2 + 71 = (n+1)(n-1) + 72, we have n + 1 | n^2 + 71 if and only if n + 1 | 72. The divisors of 72 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 72. Since n is positive, n + 1 >= 2, so n + 1 is one of 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 72, giving n = 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 11, 17, 23, 35, 71. The sum is 1+2+3+5+7+8+11+17+23+35+71 = 183.",
"check_code": "s = 0\nfor n in range(1, 10000):\n    if (n*n + 71) % (n + 1) == 0:\n        s += n\nprint(s)"
},
{
"id": "p2",
"topic": "number theory: modular arithmetic and residues (quadratic residue -1)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Find the sum of the prime numbers p ≤ 60 for which there exists an integer x such that x^2 + 1 is divisible by p.",
"answer": 197,
"target_wrong": 195,
"error_description": "The prime p = 2 is omitted (x = 1 gives 1^2 + 1 = 2); the solution lists only the primes congruent to 1 mod 4.",
"cases": ["p=2", "p=5", "p=13", "p=17", "p=29", "p=37", "p=41", "p=53"],
"solution": "We need -1 to be a quadratic residue mod p. For p = 2, x = 1 works since 2 | 2. For odd p, -1 is a quadratic residue mod p iff p ≡ 1 (mod 4) (by Euler's criterion, (-1)^((p-1)/2) = 1). The primes ≤ 60 congruent to 1 mod 4 are 5, 13, 17, 29, 37, 41, 53. Together with p = 2, the sum is 2 + 5 + 13 + 17 + 29 + 37 + 41 + 53 = 197.",
"check_code": "def isprime(p):\n    if p < 2:\n        return False\n    d = 2\n    while d * d <= p:\n        if p % d == 0:\n            return False\n        d += 1\n    return True\n\ns = 0\nfor p in range(2, 61):\n    if isprime(p) and any((x*x + 1) % p == 0 for x in range(p)):\n        s += p\nprint(s)"
},
{
"id": "p3",
"topic": "number theory: modular arithmetic and residues (divisors in a residue class)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Find the sum of the positive divisors of 945 that leave a remainder of 1 when divided by 4.",
"answer": 1320,
"target_wrong": 1131,
"error_description": "The divisor 189 = 3^3 · 7 is omitted; it is the only qualifying divisor that uses both the full power 27 and the factor 7 without 5.",
"cases": ["1", "5", "9", "21", "45", "105", "189", "945"],
"solution": "945 = 3^3 · 5 · 7, so every divisor is d = 3^i · 5^j · 7^k with 0 ≤ i ≤ 3, 0 ≤ j, k ≤ 1. Modulo 4, 3 ≡ -1, 5 ≡ 1, 7 ≡ -1, so d ≡ (-1)^(i+k) (mod 4). Thus d ≡ 1 (mod 4) iff i + k is even: (i,k) ∈ {(0,0),(1,1),(2,0),(3,1)}, each with j = 0 or 1. The divisors are 1, 5, 9, 45, 21, 105, 189, 945. Their sum is 1 + 5 + 9 + 21 + 45 + 105 + 189 + 945 = 1320.",
"check_code": "print(sum(d for d in range(1, 946) if 945 % d == 0 and d % 4 == 1))"
},
{
"id": "p4",
"topic": "number theory: modular arithmetic and residues (squares mod 10, counting pairs)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "How many ordered pairs (x, y) of integers with 1 ≤ x ≤ 20 and 1 ≤ y ≤ 20 satisfy x^2 + y^2 ≡ 0 (mod 10)?",
"answer": 72,
"target_wrong": 68,
"error_description": "The case x^2 ≡ y^2 ≡ 5 (mod 10), i.e. x and y both ending in 5, is omitted when pairing square residues 1↔9, 4↔6, 0↔0; it contributes 2·2 = 4 pairs.",
"cases": ["(x^2,y^2) ≡ (0,0): 2·2=4", "(1,9): 4·4=16", "(9,1): 4·4=16", "(4,6): 4·4=16", "(6,4): 4·4=16", "(5,5): 2·2=4"],
"solution": "Squares mod 10 depend only on the last digit: last digit 0→0, 1 or 9→1, 2 or 8→4, 3 or 7→9, 4 or 6→6, 5→5. Among 1..20 each last digit occurs twice, so the number of x with x^2 ≡ r (mod 10) is: r=0: 2, r=1: 4, r=4: 4, r=5: 2, r=6: 4, r=9: 4. We need x^2 + y^2 ≡ 0 (mod 10), so the residue pairs are (0,0), (1,9), (9,1), (4,6), (6,4), (5,5). Counting: 2·2 + 4·4 + 4·4 + 4·4 + 4·4 + 2·2 = 4 + 16 + 16 + 16 + 16 + 4 = 72.",
"check_code": "print(sum(1 for x in range(1, 21) for y in range(1, 21) if (x*x + y*y) % 10 == 0))"
},
{
"id": "p5",
"topic": "number theory: modular arithmetic and residues (digit patterns mod 7)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Find the sum of the three-digit palindromes that are divisible by 7.",
"answer": 6923,

"cases": ["161", "252", "343", "434", "525", "616", "707", "595", "686", "777", "868", "959"],
"solution": "A three-digit palindrome is aba = 101a + 10b with 1 ≤ a ≤ 9, 0 ≤ b ≤ 9. Since 101 ≡ 3 and 10 ≡ 3 (mod 7), aba ≡ 3(a + b) (mod 7), so 7 | aba iff 7 | a + b, i.e. a + b = 7 or a + b = 14. For a + b = 7: a = 1..7 gives 161, 252, 343, 434, 525, 616, 707, sum 3038. For a + b = 14: (a,b) = (5,9),(6,8),(7,7),(8,6),(9,5) gives 595, 686, 777, 868, 959, sum 3885. Total 3038 + 3885 = 6923.",
"check_code": "print(sum(n for n in range(100, 1000) if str(n) == str(n)[::-1] and n % 7 == 0))"

{
"id": "p6",
"topic": "number theory: modular arithmetic and residues (quadratic residues mod 17)",
"error_type": "omitted_case",
"question": "Find the sum of the integers a with 1 ≤ a ≤ 16 for which the congruence x^2 ≡ a (mod 17) has an integer solution x.",
"answer": 68,
"target_wrong": 55,
"error_description": "The residue 13 ≡ 8^2 = 64 (mod 17) is omitted; the solution lists the squares of 1 through 7 and stops.",

"solution": "Since x^2 ≡ (17 - x)^2, the nonzero quadratic residues mod 17 are the residues of 1^2, 2^2, ..., 8^2: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 ≡ 8, 36 ≡ 2, 49 ≡ 15, 64 ≡ 13. These are 8 distinct values (as expected, (17-1)/2 = 8). Their sum is 1 + 4 + 9 + 16 + 8 + 2 + 15 + 13 = 68. (Check: for p ≡ 1 mod 4 the quadratic residues sum to p(p-1)/4 = 17·16/4 = 68.)",
"check_code": "print(sum(a for a in range(1, 17) if any((x*x - a) % 17 == 0 for x in range(17))))"
},
{
"id": "p7",
"topic": "number theory: modular arithmetic and residues (quadratic congruence mod a prime)",
"error_type": "algebra_slip",
"question": "Find the sum of the positive integers n ≤ 100 that satisfy n^2 ≡ 2n + 15 (mod 17).",
"answer": 624,

"error_description": "Factoring n^2 - 2n - 15 as (n + 5)(n - 3) instead of (n - 5)(n + 3), giving the residue classes n ≡ 3, 12 (mod 17) instead of n ≡ 5, 14.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "Rewrite as n^2 - 2n - 15 ≡ 0 (mod 17), i.e. (n - 5)(n + 3) ≡ 0 (mod 17). Since 17 is prime, n ≡ 5 or n ≡ -3 ≡ 14 (mod 17). In 1..100: n ≡ 5: 5, 22, 39, 56, 73, 90 (sum 285); n ≡ 14: 14, 31, 48, 65, 82, 99 (sum 339). Total 285 + 339 = 624.",
"check_code": "print(sum(n for n in range(1, 101) if (n*n - 2*n - 15) % 17 == 0))"
},
{
"id": "p8",
"topic": "number theory: modular arithmetic and residues (counting in residue classes)",
"error_type": "misread_condition",
"question": "How many integers n with 1 ≤ n ≤ 1000 satisfy exactly one of the two congruences n ≡ 1 (mod 3) and n ≡ 1 (mod 5)?",
"answer": 400,
"target_wrong": 467,
"error_description": "Reading 'exactly one' as 'at least one' and computing |A ∪ B| = 334 + 200 - 67 = 467 instead of |A| + |B| - 2|A ∩ B|.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "Let A = {n ≤ 1000 : n ≡ 1 (mod 3)} and B = {n ≤ 1000 : n ≡ 1 (mod 5)}. |A| = 334 (1, 4, ..., 1000), |B| = 200 (1, 6, ..., 996). A ∩ B is n ≡ 1 (mod 15): 1, 16, ..., 991, so |A ∩ B| = 67. The number satisfying exactly one congruence is |A| + |B| - 2|A ∩ B| = 334 + 200 - 134 = 400.",
"check_code": "print(sum(1 for n in range(1, 1001) if (n % 3 == 1) != (n % 5 == 1)))"
},
{
"id": "p9",
"topic": "number theory: modular arithmetic and residues (squares ≡ 1, inclusion-exclusion)",
"error_type": "double_counting",
"question": "How many integers n with 1 ≤ n ≤ 350 satisfy n^2 ≡ 1 (mod 5) or n^2 ≡ 1 (mod 7)?",
"answer": 200,
"target_wrong": 240,
"error_description": "Adding the counts 140 (n ≡ ±1 mod 5) and 100 (n ≡ ±1 mod 7) without subtracting the 40 integers that satisfy both congruences.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "n^2 ≡ 1 (mod 5) iff n ≡ ±1 (mod 5), which is 2 of every 5 residues; since 350 = 5·70, this gives 140 values. n^2 ≡ 1 (mod 7) iff n ≡ ±1 (mod 7), 2 of every 7 residues; 350 = 7·50 gives 100 values. Both hold iff n ≡ ±1 (mod 5) and n ≡ ±1 (mod 7), which by CRT is 4 residue classes mod 35; 350 = 35·10 gives 40 values. By inclusion-exclusion the answer is 140 + 100 - 40 = 200.",
"check_code": "print(sum(1 for n in range(1, 351) if (n*n) % 5 == 1 or (n*n) % 7 == 1))"
},
{
"id": "p10",
"topic": "number theory: modular arithmetic and residues (idempotents mod 100)",
"error_type": "off_by_one",
"question": "How many integers n with 1 ≤ n ≤ 2024 satisfy n^2 ≡ n (mod 100)?",
"answer": 81,
"target_wrong": 80,
"error_description": "Counting each of the four residue classes 0, 1, 25, 76 (mod 100) as contributing exactly 20 values, missing that n = 2001 ≡ 1 (mod 100) also lies in the range.",
"cases": [],
"solution": "n^2 ≡ n (mod 100) means 100 | n(n-1). Since n and n-1 are coprime, 4 | n or 4 | n-1, and 25 | n or 25 | n-1. By CRT this gives four classes mod 100: n ≡ 0, 1, 25, 76 (mod 100). In 1 ≤ n ≤ 2024: class 0 gives 100, 200, ..., 2000 (20 values); class 1 gives 1, 101, ..., 2001 (21 values); class 25 gives 25, ..., 1925 (20 values, since 2025 > 2024); class 76 gives 76, ..., 1976 (20 values). Total 20 + 21 + 20 + 20 = 81.",
"check_code": "print(sum(1 for n in range(1, 2025) if (n*n - n) % 100 == 0))"
}
]}
